description: Curated multi-level question taxonomy assignments for GATE CSE (pilot cross-topic indexing)

go:333214.rationale: GATE CSE 2020 Q17 evaluates the probability that a randomly chosen binary relation on a 3-element set is reflexive (2^6 / 2^9 = 1/8 = 0.125). It bridges combinatorial probability with reflexive relation counting.
go:333214.syllabusRef: GATE 2025 CSE Section 1 (Engineering Mathematics / Discrete Mathematics)

go:1075.rationale: GATE CSE 2004 Q81 examines intersection and union connectivity of graphs on the same vertex set. If G1 ∩ G2 is disconnected, then G1 ∪ G2 must contain a cycle. It bridges algorithm graph properties with discrete mathematics graph connectivity.
go:1075.syllabusRef: GATE 2025 CSE Section 1 (Discrete Mathematics) and Section 2 (Algorithms)

go:1073.rationale: GATE CSE 2004 Q79 asks for the number of simple graphs on n labeled vertices having at least (n^2 - 3n)/2 edges. Out of N = C(n,2) = (n^2 - n)/2 possible edges, selecting at least (n^2 - 3n)/2 is equivalent to omitting at most n edges, giving sum_{k=0}^n C(N, k) (Option D). It bridges combinatorics and counting with graph theory.
go:1073.syllabusRef: GATE 2025 CSE Section 1 (Discrete Mathematics: Combinatorics and Graph Theory)

go:1371.rationale: Counts distinct binary search tree structures on 4 distinct keys (C_4 = 14) under Programming & Data Structures (Binary Search Tree), evaluated via Catalan numbers under Combinatorics.
go:1371.syllabusRef: GATE CSE Section 2 (Programming and Data Structures / Trees)
